title: Normal Accident Theory Crisis Communication
transcript: in 1984 sociologist Charles perau introduced the normal accident Theory Nat is a framework for understanding how accidents can occur in complex systems in fact how complex systems are more likely than less complex systems to experience sudden catastrophic failure this is due to the inherent complexities and tight couplings of the systems components here are some of the key concepts of Gat one complex interactions pero emphasizes that the different parts of a complex system often interact in unpredictable in incomprehensible ways in systems with complex interactions it's hard to anticipate how different elements will behave together especially under unusual conditions the United States government for example is a complex system a priority shift in the House of Representatives could trigger changes in the behavior of the White House or the Supreme Court and even local governments two tight versus loose coupling coupling refers to the degree of dependence between different parts of a system in tightly coupled systems processes occur in a strict sequence with little room for adjustment or delay in Loosely coupled systems there's more flexibility and buffer space tight coupling in complex systems can exacerbate problems as a failure in one part quickly propagates to other parts still other systems like for example the United States government oscillate from loose to tight during election Seasons or when a president is nearing the end of their final term in office or when we are at War the system tightens up and becomes more prone to failure three inevitability of accidents natat posits that with highly complex tightly coupled systems accidents are not just possible possible but inevitable the unpredictability within such systems the inconceivable number of interactions and tight linkages make it impossible to foresee and guard against all potential failures this inevitability according to the theory must be conceded and embraced four limits of safety measures according to natat while safety measures and redundancies are important they will inevitably be limited in their capacity to prevent accidents in reality the act of adding safety features and protocols will actually increase complexity potentially introducing new Pathways to failure five system design considerations perro suggests that to minimize accidents systems should be designed with simpler interactions and looser couplings whenever possible this is different from other models of Crisis management which attempt to predict and institutionalize very specific plans to manage very specific crises thanks for listening
